Drupal published security advisory SA-CORE-2026-017 on November 18 for CVE-2026-132165 — a remote code execution flaw in the installer, install.php, that lets an unauthenticated attacker attempt to reinstall Drupal under specific conditions and take over the site. Drupal rates it highly critical, 20 out of 25. Affected: versions below 10.6.22, 11.0 through 11.3.21, and 11.4.0 through 11.4.12; the fix is in 10.6.22, 11.3.22 and 11.4.13. It was discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner. Exploitation on live sites was reported as early as November 19 at 19:00 UTC — the day after the advisory. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on November 24, with a federal remediation deadline of November 27 — three days.

Two things to keep straight. First, the 9.8 CVSS score you will see in some reporting is not in Drupal's advisory — it comes from secondary reporting and NVD, so I am not attributing it to Drupal. Second, if you cannot upgrade immediately, block access to /core/install.php in your web-server configuration; that is the mitigation Drupal itself gives. The installer is the page that builds the site, and it was reachable by anyone, doing the one thing it should never do after setup: run again.

The installer builds your site. Left open, it rebuilds it for someone else.

Palo Alto Networks published advisory PAN-SA-2026-0015 on November 25 for Fragnesia, CVE-2026-46300 — a Linux kernel privilege-escalation flaw in the XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem, first disclosed in May 2026. On its own it needs a local foothold. The campaign chained it with PHP2Shell, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, PHP flaws that give remote code execution through the PAN-OS management web server — and then Fragnesia escalates that to root, all in a single HTTP request. Dream reported on October 26 that a Chinese-speaking, suspected China-nexus actor compromised 25 servers — 24 firewalls and one internal firewall management server — including two servers belonging to a U.S. government-affiliated organization, in an AI-assisted campaign on October 23–24. Palo Alto's Unit 42 verified the findings on October 29. The fix builds are out now, and Palo Alto says the only known PAN-OS route requires first exploiting PHP2Shell through an internet-exposed management interface — if you are running a fixed PAN-OS from the PHP2Shell advisory, you are protected.

I want to be precise about where the attribution comes from: the China link and the AI-assisted description are Dream's assessment, verified in scope by Palo Alto — Palo Alto's own advisory names no actor and does not mention AI. The number that should stay with you is the exposure figure Unit 42 gave: about 0.02 percent of customer devices worldwide had management interfaces exposed to the internet and were affected. Small in percentage, and every one of them was a firewall whose management plane was reachable from anywhere. The PHP2Shell patches were out by October 30; the Fragnesia fix lands today. If your management interface faces the internet, the patch is not the first thing to fix — the exposure is.

The management interface is the firewall's front door. It was facing the street.

19 years of BitLocker lockout just collapsed to 20 days because of a $1 motherboard flash chip.

Firmware TPMs on modern laptops store failed PIN counts on external SPI flash. TPM 2.0 Dictionary Attack Protection enforces a 32-try limit followed by one guess every 10 minutes, relying on a JEDEC counter called RPMC inside that flash chip to stop state rollbacks.

 At ACM CCS 2026, researchers broke that lock on both sides.
On Winbond RPMC flash (25R and 74M chips), a 1-second voltage glitch leaks the HMAC signing key straight out of the chip. Any laptop using that flash, Intel or AMD, now accepts forged counter values and rolls back its failed-attempt state.

On AMD fTPM (CVE-2026-43613), the firmware skips verifying whether the counter ever incremented. A custom interposer sitting between the CPU and SPI flash blocks counter updates with zero glitching.

 Measured worst-case brute-force results on locked laptops:
  * 4-digit Windows Hello PIN: 69 days down to 40 hours
  * 6-digit BitLocker startup PIN: 19 years down to 20 days

Winbond has no patch timeline because fixing the leak takes new silicon. AMD published AMD-SB-7079 with firmware fixes rolling out from November 2026 through February 2027.

Researchers used a flash-chip interposer to bypass TPM lockout and guess Hello and BitLocker PINs in lab tests; AMD tracks CVE-2026-43613 (CVSS 5.1). Check devices for tampering; lengthen PINs.

#DFIR_Radar https://t.co/biVpToWOIU

Your PC has a mechanism that remembers every incorrect PIN attempt and eventually locks you out

Researchers at TU Berlin found a way to make that mechanism forget

Their attack, called Hello Again, targets the Replay Protected Monotonic Counters (RPMC) used to protect security state stored in motherboard flash memory

The TPM relies on this state to remember failed authentication attempts and prevent brute-force guessing

The researchers found two ways to undermine that protection:

On affected AMD systems, they intercepted communication between the processor and flash chip, suppressing counter updates while making the processor believe they succeeded
On systems using vulnerable Winbond flash chips, voltage glitching exposed a cryptographic key that allowed the researchers to forge counter values

With the lockout state repeatedly reset, they could automate PIN guesses without the normal security delays

Their laboratory demonstrations included:

A four-digit Windows Hello PIN found in 57 minutes, with a worst-case estimated search time of 40 hours instead of 69 days
A six-digit BitLocker startup PIN found in under seven minutes, with a worst-case estimate of 20 days instead of 19 years

The attack required physical access, specialised hardware and vulnerable hardware configurations

It also affects different platforms for different reasons

AMD assigned its firmware issue CVE-2026-43613 and is planning firmware fixes extending into February 2027

Intel says the research did not demonstrate a vulnerability in Intel components; the tested Intel system depended on a flaw in its third-party Winbond flash chip

For now, researchers recommend using longer PINs, adding at least two digits where possible

The deeper security lesson is that a PIN's strength depends not only on how difficult it is to guess, but also on whether the hardware enforcing guess limits can be trusted

The campaign exploited PHP2Shell vulnerabilities CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, with an operator adapting public proofs of concept on the day they appeared. The custom exploit reportedly worked against default PHP/Apache configurations: a multipart POST with more than 1,000 fields and excessive header lines exhausted PHP’s memory limit, while a second request on the same keep-alive connection used residual session state to leak memory and invoke `system`. The exploit supported PHP builds through per-version calibration, but patched releases stopped the chain. The reported fixes are PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.12.

The operator fingerprinted PHP/Apache hosts using Shodan, narrowing a pool of 68,198 hosts to a shortlist of about 5,042. The campaign targeted 595 unique IPs across 57 countries; 404 hosts were assessed as compromised, with approximately 290,000 files (9.5 GB) collected. Exploitation and collection were organized through a job-based C2 and an AI-agent system: a custom queue dispatched 39 workers backed by two self-hosted DeepSeek endpoints. The evidence indicates human-directed, AI-assisted operations; complete autonomous execution was not established.

Post-compromise activity included reverse shells, SSH-key installation, periodic beacons, token-protected PHP webshells, cron persistence, and localhost-only Dropbear tunnels. Collection scripts inventoried hosts, searched repositories for secrets, gathered database backups and application data, and harvested cloud credentials, OAuth tokens, session files, and source code. Stolen credentials enabled cloud enumeration and further access attempts. A separate financial-fraud effort reached withdrawal and account-takeover capabilities, but no cryptocurrency theft was confirmed; an unauthenticated Redis instance did yield about 3.3 million user records.

Defenders should investigate suspicious high-volume multipart PHP requests followed by a same-connection request, web-server processes spawning shells or download tools, new SSH keys, unauthorized PHP prepend directives, Dropbear on loopback, and outbound traffic to the reported C2 on port 8088 or reverse-shell ports 41000–49153. Patching alone is insufficient after compromise: affected hosts require investigation or reimaging, and exposed credentials should be rotated. The report does not attribute the activity to a known threat group.

An attacker patched a vulnerability on its own relay server. That is the detail I keep coming back to in GreyNoise's writeup of the Check Point campaign.

GreyNoise tracked an intrusion campaign against Check Point Security Management Servers hitting at least 22 organizations between October 17 and November 2. The actor used a compromised server as an operational relay, staging stolen firewall databases and internal CA files there.

By early November, other threat actors were scanning the relay. The actor ran a check for CVE-2026-98432, a Linux IPv4 use-after-free, then used nftables to drop the packet types that trigger it. Per GreyNoise: 'This allowed the actor to protect their hop from others engaging in future exploitation of the bug.'

Defender takeaway: attacker infrastructure gets patch hygiene too, and that shows up on your side. Unexpected nftables rules on a server nobody should be tuning, or an entry in /etc/ld.so.preload, are worth alerting on. The victims here only got identified because the actor's automation failed and shipped error output back to the hop.

Злоумышленники использовали многочисленные уязвимости для взлома двух десятков серверов управления Check Point Security в рамках продолжающейся кампании, направленной на 22 организации.

Активность выявила GreyNoise, отметившая, что она напоминает операции кибершпионажа, хотя мотивы злоумышленника окончательно установить не удалось.

Исследователи отслеживают активность под номером GT13 и подтвердили, что она продолжалась с 17 октября по 2 ноября, после чего их наблюдение прекратилось.

Однако, учитывая постоянный доступ злоумышленника к устройствам Check Point, они считают, что кампания остается активной.

По данным GreyNoise, 22 организации-жертвы расположены в 17 странах, среди которых госучреждения, поставщики финансовых услуг, а также компании энергетического, транспортного, горнодобывающего и производственного секторов.

Атаки были совершены с 99 IP, которые, судя по всему, принадлежат скомпрометированным устройствам Check Point и выходным узлам ExpressVPN.

Файловый HTTP-сервер Rejetto, скомпрометированный с помощью CVE-2026-61500, использовался в качестве оперативного ретранслятора для управления вторжениями и сбора украденных данных из скомпрометированных сред.

GreyNoise пока не смогла установить, когда и как были взломаны серверы Check Point, но зафиксировала использование CVE-2026-16232 на этапах после взлома.

Уязвимость связана с обходом аутентификации в Check Point SmartConsole, которая позволяет злоумышленникам получить токен для входа в приложение и пройти аутентификацию с правами администратора.

В свою очередь, Check Point предупредила о ней еще в июле, обозначив ее как активно используемую 0-day.

Исследователи также зафиксировали попытки использования CVE-2025-5777 (Citrix NetScaler), CVE-2024-21893 (Ivanti), CVE-2026-41089 (Windows NetLogon), CVE-2026-16232 (Check Point SmartConsole) и CVE-2026-98432 (Linux IPv4 UAF).

26 октября злоумышленник провел операцию по массовому управлению сертификатами на всех 24 скомпрометированных серверах Check Point, которая завершилась неудачей, но зато помогла GreyNoise идентифицировать жертв.

Исследователи пришли к выводу, что GT13 использовала инструмент нападения на основе ИИ, основываясь на поведении, наблюдаемой автоматизации и специально разработанных инструментах, однако использование ИИ в этой кампании остается неподтвержденным.

Учитывая, что кампания все еще может быть активной, GreyNoise поделилась IOCs, которые могут помочь выявить дополнительные вторжения или заблокировать будущие попытки.

Представители Check Point заявляют, что им известно о действиях, описанных в отчете GreyNoise.

По их данным, злоумышленники использовали CVE-2026-16232, позволяющую обойти аутентификацию SmartConsole, о которой Check Point публично сообщила в июле 2026 года, отметив, что эксплуатация уже наблюдалась в реальных условиях.

Таким образом, эта уязвимость и доступные средства защиты не являются новыми. Злоумышленники также использовали адаптированный общедоступный модуль Metasploit для CVE-2026-16232, поэтому метод эксплуатации уже был известен ранее.

В общем, будем следить.

Disclosed November 17 — I am dating this one plainly because it is nine days old — Java4Shell is CVE-2026-114938, a heap overflow in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder on x86-64 systems with AVX-512 VBMI instructions, scored 8.1. It affects Java 17, 21, 25 and 27; ARM64 is unaffected. The researcher found it with AI assistance in late October. Fixed versions are out — 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1 and 27.0.1.1 — and there is a mitigation flag if you cannot upgrade immediately.

Two things to keep in proportion. There is no confirmed exploitation in the wild as of November 18. And the researcher's claim of pre-authentication remote code execution against default configurations of several Java products is not independently verified, and the chains have not been publicly released. So this is not a fire — it is a flaw in a decoder that sits in front of a very large number of applications, with a fix already available. That is the kind of thing patch windows exist for.

Nine days old, no exploitation seen, and still worth the patch window.

As of Nov 26, Salus has tracked 13 vulnerabilities that exchanges, wallets and node operators should check now. Most of them hit HTTP/2 entry points and PHP: API gateways, public RPC endpoints and web backends. Grouped by component, they come down to 7 upgrades.

1 | NGINX (CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633)

Two HTTP/2 bugs: memory corruption in the send window and a use-after-free on connection release. Affects open source 1.9.5–1.31.8 and some NGINX Plus releases. Check public TLS + HTTP/2 endpoints and reverse proxies first.

Fix: open source 1.30.7 / 1.31.9+, NGINX Plus 37.0.8.1 / 37.3.0.1+. If you can't upgrade yet, disable HTTP/2 and make sure old worker processes have exited.

2 | Apache HTTP Server (CVE-2026-119618)

HTTP/2 heap memory corruption. Affects 2.4.55–2.4.70 and standalone mod_h2 2.0.8–2.0.42.

Fix: 2.4.71+, and update standalone mod_h2 too. If you can't upgrade yet, disable HTTP/2 and keep HTTP/1.1.

3 | PHP (5 vulnerabilities)

CVE-2026-129289 PHP-FPM FastCGI request smuggling
CVE-2026-129496 Timezone cache use-after-free
CVE-2026-126714 Partial session file overwrite
CVE-2026-115560 Session serialization format mismatch
CVE-2026-129474 Error backtrace use-after-free (8.5 only)

Fix: 8.2.36 / 8.3.37 / 8.4.28 / 8.5.13+, then restart the master and all worker processes. If you can't upgrade yet, turn off backend connection reuse to PHP-FPM (on NGINX, keep fastcgi_keep_conn off). On 8.5, set zend.exception_ignore_args=1.

4 | Vite dev server RCE (GHSA-p4f5-76q4-ffq7)

Affects multiple vite branches from 4.0.0 to 8.3.6, and vite-plus 1.5.0 and earlier. Highest risk: wallet and DApp dev servers exposed to the network.

Fix: 6.4.6 / 7.3.8 / 8.1.7 / 8.2.5 / 8.3.7+, vite-plus 1.5.1+, and update your lockfile. If you can't upgrade yet, bind the dev server to localhost only.

5 | OpenJDK "Java4Shell" (CVE-2026-114938)

Out-of-bounds write in Base64 decoding. Affects Java services that decode external Base64 on x86-64 hosts with AVX-512 VBMI, across JDK 17, 21, 25 and 27.

Fix: Oracle JDK 17.0.21.1 / 21.0.13.1 / 25.0.5.1 / 27.0.1.1+. Temurin and Corretto users should follow the build numbers in their vendor advisories, then restart the JVM. If you can't upgrade yet, set -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics.

6 | OpenSSH password auth bypass (CVE-2026-123158)

Affects versions before 10.6p2 on musl libc systems without PAM that allow password login. Check Alpine ops hosts and nodes first.

Fix: 10.6p2+. On Alpine, install the fixed packages in 3.21.10 / 3.22.8 / 3.23.8 / 3.24.4. If you can't upgrade yet, confirm key login works, then disable password login.

7 | Ruby (CVE-2026-132825, GHSA-87fm-7w84-j2px)

Heap overflow and integer overflow in string case conversion. Affects 3.3.13 and earlier, 3.4.0–3.4.12 and 4.0.0–4.0.9.

Fix: 3.3.14 / 3.4.13 / 4.0.10+, then restart apps and background jobs.

One last thing: restart after upgrading and confirm the old processes are gone. Plenty of "patched" services are still running the old version.

The report describes misuse of ARTEX, an LLM-powered penetration-testing framework, across several campaigns. Reported activity includes attacks against South Korean financial organizations, Japanese companies, IT and software vendors, and financial-sector targets. The operators remain unknown in the Korean and Japanese cases; the report treats them as separate intrusions and does not infer shared attribution from overlapping infrastructure. Storm-0940 activity involved password spraying and abuse of ConnectWise Cloud Backup-related access. Storm-3358 activity involved financial-sector targeting and infrastructure associated with WISP. Other reported tools include vshell and AdaptixC2.

Common behaviors include rapid reconnaissance of web and API surfaces; enumeration of distinct customer or application records; probing authentication, SSO, OAuth, and application endpoints; and password spraying with rotating user agents. Other patterns include repeated requests with altered headers or tokens, SSRF attempts using redirecting URLs to reach internal or metadata addresses, and downloading exposed configuration or backup files. Cloud activity includes exposed-secret use, service-principal sign-ins, OAuth credential addition, and credential discovery across AWS services. The report also describes upload-then-execute behavior and self-correcting API retries, including retries after HTTP 422 responses.

The detection approach prioritizes behavior over framework-specific strings, which can be changed or generated by the model. Proposed rules correlate sequences such as multiple distinct reconnaissance requests within a short window, high-volume record access, and file uploads followed by execution. ARTEX-specific headers, user agents, webshell keys, response markers, domains, and IP addresses are treated as supporting indicators; shared infrastructure and generic user agents require caution. Reported Windows artifacts include files named in an intent-ID/purpose/extension format and paths under `C:\Windows\Temp` or `C:\ProgramData`; these are described as renameable indicators rather than durable detections.

The report recommends correlating network telemetry with identity and cloud logs. Zeek can identify indicators and behavioral sequences in DNS, connection, and decrypted HTTP data, while cloud and identity rules cover activity not visible at the network perimeter. IP-based indicators may be reassigned or shared, so the report advises against blocking them automatically; some generic indicators are enrichment-only. It also notes a known gap: password spraying distributed across many source IPs can evade per-IP thresholds.

Researchers observed autonomous AI agents exploiting default credentials and CVE-2025-3248 across internet-exposed LiteLLM, Dify, and Langflow deployments — harvesting API keys at over 69 requests per minute and immediately reusing stolen credentials to fund further reconnaissance. GreyNoise observed an intrusion campaign attributed to the untracked actor GT13 against Check Point Security Management Servers from October 17 to November 2, 2026. At least 22 organizations across multiple regions and sectors were affected. The actor used Nmap, Chisel, Impacket, Paramiko, and custom Python scripts for exploitation, internal reconnaissance, credential discovery, privilege escalation attempts, and lateral movement.

The actor first compromised an HFS server using CVE-2026-61500. By collecting session cookies generated through HFS’s `loginSrp1` endpoint, they reconstructed the V8 pseudorandom-number generator state, recovered the signing key, and forged an administrator cookie. The cookie allowed access from a different IP address. The compromised server was then prepared as an operational relay: the actor attempted to install malware, created an unauthenticated HTTP file-upload service, and configured Chisel as a reverse proxy.

From this relay, GT13 accessed Check Point environments and used a script for CVE-2026-16232, an authentication bypass that enables command execution through SmartConsole. The actor launched more than 100 management tasks, attempted to copy firewall databases and Internal CA files, and generated a certificate named `pivot.p12`. They also attempted to unload security policies, which could disable firewalls, and probed systems including Citrix NetScaler, Ivanti Connect Secure, VMware vCenter, Microsoft Exchange, Oracle TNS, and domain controllers. Scripts performed broad port scanning and SSH credential attempts using victim-themed usernames and passwords.

Other vulnerabilities the actor used or attempted to exploit included CVE-2025-5777, CVE-2024-21893, CVE-2026-41089, and CVE-2026-98432. On the relay, GT13 checked for the Linux IPv4 use-after-free vulnerability CVE-2026-98432 and attempted to mitigate it with `nftables` rules dropping IPv4 packets containing IP options.

The actor already had Check Point access before the HFS compromise, and how they got it is unknown. Persistent access suggests the campaign is ongoing.

- Relay build: on 2026-10-02 the actor hit Rejetto HFS with CVE-2026-61500. Repeated POSTs to loginSrp1 leaked sid values from Math.random(), enough to rebuild V8 PRNG state, recover the cookie signing key, and forge an admin session. Bulk results from 24 compromised Check Point servers landed in /root/exfil/pc_<victim IP>.txt. Each server pushed its file via scp, so each holds the SSH private key matching the key planted on the hop.

CVE-2023-46805 enables authentication bypass, while CVE-2024-21887 allows command injection; chained exploitation can provide unauthenticated remote code execution with elevated privileges. Investigations found attackers harvesting credentials stored on the gateways, including cached Active Directory administrator credentials, cleartext passwords and NTLM hashes associated with active sessions, and credentials recovered from database backups. They have used appliance-native tools and libraries, including FreeRDP, SSH, Telnet, and Nmap, for internal reconnaissance and lateral movement; some incidents resulted in domain compromise. Observed post-exploitation activity also included deploying a Sliver implant.

CISA research demonstrated that root-level access could be used to establish persistence that survives factory resets and upgrades. Persistence stored on an encrypted drive partition may evade integrity checks. CISA investigations found web shells on devices that the Ivanti Integrity Checker Tool (ICT) reported as having no file mismatches. Attackers were also observed overwriting and time-stomping files and remounting the runtime partition, further obscuring evidence of compromise. Therefore, a clean ICT result or device reset does not reliably establish that an appliance is uncompromised.

Defenders should treat credentials stored on affected appliances as potentially exposed, hunt for malicious activity, apply available Ivanti updates, and assess the risk of continued appliance use. Recommended exposure-reduction measures include restricting appliance outbound connections to required services and limiting VPN access to unprivileged accounts.

What AI Models Are Actually Finding
The evidence base distinguishes three tiers of AI-discovered vulnerability claims, and they carry different confidence levels.

The first tier — software and library vulnerabilities — is well-documented. Google GTIG tracked 2,076 AI-related CVEs between January 2025 and August 2026, with more than 1,500 in 2026 alone, roughly half affecting AI orchestration frameworks [Source: SecurityWeek / Google GTIG, Sep 30, 2026]. One named example, CVE-2026-1731, was an unauthenticated OS command injection flaw in BeyondTrust Privileged Remote Access discovered autonomously by the Hacktron AI research agent; one threat cluster exploited it within four days of public disclosure, and five more followed within seven days [Source: SecurityWeek / Google GTIG, Sep 30, 2026]. The Axios reporting on early testing of new frontier models describes Cisco and Zscaler using them internally to "chain together vulnerabilities to build an exploit chain" — the shift from single-bug discovery to multi-step attack path construction [Source: Axios, Apr 21, 2026].

The second tier — kernel and root-access flaws — is documented at one confirmed instance. Between April 29 and May 13, 2026, three publicly disclosed flaws gave local users a path to root access across major Linux distributions. Microsoft confirmed that AI found the "Copy Fail" vulnerability among them, and assessed that "the other two fit the same broader pattern, suggesting that AI will increase the pace at which serious vulnerability classes are discovered" [Source: Microsoft MDDR, Oct 9, 2026]. Kernel-level access is the layer immediately above hardware — it controls hardware, memory, and system processes. An attacker who compromises the kernel gains, in Microsoft's words, "total dominion over the system." This is the closest documented open-source analogue to what Altman describes as "hardware-level, insane stuff."

The third tier — structurally unpatchable hardware vulnerabilities, Altman's specific claim — is where open-source evidence runs thin. The Mother Jones piece notes that a PHP vulnerability type had been "noted decades ago, but the flaw had been considered too difficult to exploit and was largely forgotten until August [2026], when researchers using new models found a way to exploit it" [Source: Mother Jones, Oct 21, 2026]. This describes a class of vulnerability where the flaw was known but assumed to be beyond exploitation — AI changed the feasibility calculation, not the patching requirement. That is distinct from hardware bugs that physically cannot be patched. Altman's statement remains the primary public evidence for the hardware-unpatchable category; no independent technical source corroborates it with specifics in the collected evidence. 1/6

Fix: 6.4.6 / 7.3.8 / 8.1.7 / 8.2.5 / 8.3.7+, vite-plus 1.5.1+, and update your lockfile. If you can't upgrade yet, bind the dev server to localhost only.

5 | OpenJDK "Java4Shell" (CVE-2026-114938)

Out-of-bounds write in Base64 decoding. Affects Java services that decode external Base64 on x86-64 hosts with AVX-512 VBMI, across JDK 17, 21, 25 and 27.

Fix: Oracle JDK 17.0.21.1 / 21.0.13.1 / 25.0.5.1 / 27.0.1.1+. Temurin and Corretto users should follow the build numbers in their vendor advisories, then restart the JVM. If you can't upgrade yet, set -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics.

6 | OpenSSH password auth bypass (CVE-2026-123158)

Affects versions before 10.6p2 on musl libc systems without PAM that allow password login. Check Alpine ops hosts and nodes first.

Fix: 10.6p2+. On Alpine, install the fixed packages in 3.21.10 / 3.22.8 / 3.23.8 / 3.24.4. If you can't upgrade yet, confirm key login works, then disable password login.

7 | Ruby (CVE-2026-132825, GHSA-87fm-7w84-j2px)

Heap overflow and integer overflow in string case conversion. Affects 3.3.13 and earlier, 3.4.0–3.4.12 and 4.0.0–4.0.9.

Fix: 3.3.14 / 3.4.13 / 4.0.10+, then restart apps and background jobs.

One last thing: restart after upgrading and confirm the old processes are gone. Plenty of "patched" services are still running the old version.

vulnerabilities.description: MONEO ERP exposes the Ping method of its slave JSON-RPC service over WebSocket as @rpc.openpublic, so it can be called without a valid session. The method's only guard compares the calling application name with " login", but that value is taken from the client-controlled params.appname field of the request. When the check passes, Ping stores an attacker-chosen session ID, user number and company in the server session store, and subsequent session validation accepts that session. An unauthenticated remote attacker can therefore create a valid session as any user, including administrators, in any company (tenant) hosted on the server and invoke authenticated RPC methods with that user's privileges, gaining read and write access to that company's data.

A security vulnerability has been detected in WOW-CMS BlizzCMS up to 1.2.1. Affected is the function Home::setconfig of the file application/modules/home/controllers/Home.php of the component Home Module. The manipulation leads to improper authorization. The attack can be initiated remotely.

The backend language switch action (quick change language) of the JTL-Shop administration backend is executed without a CSRF token check, and the supplied language value is neither validated against the installed backend languages nor encoded on output. The value is stored in the session and in the account data of the administrator and rendered without output encoding in JavaScript strings and HTML attributes of backend pages. An unauthenticated remote attacker can thereby cause script code to be executed in the browser of a logged-in administrator who opens a crafted web page; the code can perform actions with the privileges of that administrator.

The OPC (OnPage Composer) start menu, which JTL-Shop shows to logged-in backend users on storefront pages, writes the current page identifier (which contains the search term on search pages) and further values into single-quoted JavaScript strings without escaping. A single quote in the search term terminates the string. An unauthenticated remote attacker can thereby cause script code to be executed in the browser of a backend user who opens a crafted link while logged in to the backend in the same browser; the code runs with the privileges of that user and can use the backend session token contained in the same script to send requests to the backend. Visitors and customers do not receive the start menu and are not affected.

A vulnerability was determined in eosphoros-ai DB-GPT up to 0.8.2. The affected element is the function editor sql run of the file packages/dbgpt-app/src/dbgpt app/openapi/api v1/editor/api editor v1.py. Lookyloo is a web-based malware analysis and sandboxing platform. The pull-from-remote-instance feature allows a user to request a previously captured sample from another Lookyloo instance by specifying the target instance's URL and a capture UUID. Prior to the fix, the only restriction on the target URL was a check that the hostname, if it was a literal IP address, was not in a private range. Hostnames that resolved to private or internal addresses were not blocked, and no authentication or allowlist was enforced for anonymous users. This allowed any unauthenticated user to direct the Lookyloo server to issue HTTP requests (HEAD to the root path and GET to /json/<uuid>/status, followed by a capture download) to arbitrary internal or external hosts, effectively enabling a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attack. An attacker could use this to probe internal network topology, access captures stored on internal Lookyloo instances, or leverage the server as a proxy to reach otherwise unreachable services. The vulnerability is in the website/web/ init .py module, specifically the  get remote capture function and the associated pull endpoint. The security impact is unauthorized disclosure of capture data and internal service information from Lookyloo instances that are not intended to be publicly accessible.

The Database for Contact Form 7, WPforms, Elementor forms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.5 via the copy files function. This is due to missing file extension validation in the copy files function, which accepts attacker-controlled stream wrapper URIs as the file source and derives the destination filename without restricting executable extensions. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. The plugin places an .htaccess file in its uploads directory to block PHP execution, but this mitigation is ineffective on Nginx, LiteSpeed in certain configurations, and Apache servers with AllowOverride None, and the file is not restored if deleted.

A successful exploit could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands within the context of the system. This vulnerability affects OpenScape 4000, versions V11 R0.22 through V11 R2.11 and V10 R1.68 and earlier, and OpenScape 4000 Manager, versions V11 R0.22 through V11 R2.11 and V10 R1.34 through V10 R1.68. The country manager page of the JTL-Shop administration backend (/admin/countries) writes the request parameter activeSortOrder without output encoding into a single-quoted JavaScript string and into HTML attributes. The overview page requires no CSRF token. An unauthenticated remote attacker can thereby cause script code to be executed in the browser of a logged-in backend user who opens a crafted link in the same browser (the session cookie carries no SameSite attribute by default); the code runs with the privileges of that user and can use the backend token of the same page to send requests to the backend. D-Link DWM-222W developed by D-Link Corporation has a Use of Hard-coded Credentials vulnerability. Unauthenticated adjacent network attackers can use the administrator account embedded in the firmware to access the configuration backup endpoint and obtain plaintext passwords for all user accounts.

Flowintel contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in its HedgeDoc case-notes integration. When a user with editor or administrator privileges associates a HedgeDoc URL with a case, the application later issues a server-side HTTP GET request to that URL to retrieve note content. Before the fix, the stored URL was used directly without validation of its scheme, host, port, path, or userinfo, and the HTTP client followed redirects by default with no connect or read timeouts.

An authenticated attacker could therefore cause the Flowintel server to issue requests to arbitrary internal or external endpoints (for example, cloud instance-metadata services, internal management interfaces, or other intranet hosts) and receive the response body, or follow a redirect chain to an unintended destination. The absence of timeouts also permitted resource-exhaustion against the server's outbound connection pool.

Preconditions:
- An authenticated account with editor or administrator role on the target case.
- The HedgeDoc integration feature is enabled (no explicit configuration gate existed before the fix).

Impact:
- Disclosure of sensitive data served by internal or cloud-metadata endpoints.
- Potential denial of service through unbounded outbound requests.

Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

The Sneeit Framework plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in versions up to, and including, 8.7 via the 'callback' parameter of the sneeit compact menu mega content AJAX action. The handler sneeit compact menu mega content callback() is registered on the wp ajax nopriv hook and passes the attacker-supplied 'callback' value directly into call user func() after only a function exists() check, with the single argument also attacker-controlled via a JSON-decoded 'args' parameter. There is no authentication, no capability check, no nonce, and no allow-list of callable functions. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary existing PHP/WordPress functions with controlled arguments.

A vulnerability was detected in bayang jelu up to 0.88.2. The manipulation results in missing authorization. The attack can be launched remotely. Upgrading to version 0.88.3 addresses this issue. A **NULL pointer dereference** flaw has been found in the vlv value compare() function in vlv pagination.c of the Virtual List View module in the **Samba** package. The function uses the sort value from the search result with no check that the result still contains that attribute. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can search the directory sends a Virtual List View search by value, sorted on an attribute the matching entries do not have. The LDAP worker that handles the search exits, which disconnects the directory clients that were using that worker, and the directory service starts a replacement worker. Another search of the same kind crashes the worker that accepts it, and each further crash waits longer before that worker is replaced, so repeating the search keeps the LDAP service from staying available. The same crash follows a search sorted on an attribute the attacker is not allowed to read. The directory removes that attribute from the result, and the comparison uses the missing value.

In RealVNC Server before 7.19.1, UDP-based connections could potentially be exploited without authentication to execute code remotely or cause the software to crash. In Eclipse Dataspace Components (EDC) Connector 1.0.0-RC2 through 1.0.0-RC7, the HashiCorp Vault extension does not reject .. path segments in secret aliases. In a multi-participant (virtual) control plane where vault partitions share the runtime's Vault token, an authenticated participant can set a callback secret alias that escapes its own vault partition. The connector then reads secrets of other participants or of the runtime, such as STS client secrets or the encryption key, and sends them to an endpoint the attacker chooses.

A crafted byte stream can be parsed as one message by this tolerant parser and as a different message by a strict ASCII-armor parser. The strict mode is opt-in; the default parser remains tolerant.

Upstream reports that the Nettle and OpenSSL backends, including the default Nettle build, accept this key. Under that key, a signature can verify for every message. The access rules of JTL-Shop (export/.htaccess and export/backup/.htaccess) release files with the extensions gz and zip for the export directory without withdrawing this release in the subdirectory export/backup, in which the shop stores database dumps and file backups. As a result, backup files in this directory can be downloaded without authentication by anyone who knows or guesses the file name. Up to version 5.5.5 the names of database backups consist only of a timestamp; from version 5.6.0 they contain a random component, which does not replace access control. The backups contain the complete shop database (customer data, orders, password hashes) and, for file backups, files of the shop. The access rules are only evaluated by Apache. On installations where another web server, for example nginx, delivers static files such as gz and zip directly (including nginx in front of Apache), the files remain accessible even with the corrected rules, unless the directory is blocked at server level.

impacts: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
vulnerabilities.description: In Eclipse Krazo Extensions up to and including 3.0.0, AsciiDocViewEngine passes MVC model values to Asciidoctor as document attributes without encoding them. Asciidoctor substitutes attribute references after it escapes HTML special characters and before it processes inline macros. As a result, attacker-controlled model values end up in the output as raw HTML and can inject AsciiDoc inline macros. This allows cross-site scripting in applications that render untrusted data through AsciiDoc views.
